adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx:34 — Removing the Ruler-API query eliminates the previous fallback where rules from the Ruler response were still rendered if the Prometheus query failed (old check was `!rulerResponse && !promResponse`), so a Prometheus API failure is now a single point of failure for the whole group instead of degrading gracefully.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the Ruler API query entirely in `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx` (deleted `useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery` and all rendering based on `rulerResponse?.rules`). The error/empty-state check changes from `if (!rulerResponse && !promResponse)` to `if (!promResponse)`, so if the Prometheus query fails/returns no data, the component now shows the error Alert and renders nothing else. Previously, if `promResponse` was missing but `rulerResponse` existed, it would still render list items from `rulerResponse` (often with `operation={Creating}` when no matching prom rule). This is a real resilience/fallback regression, but given the stated goal in comments elsewhere (“removed all requests to the ruler API in the list view”), it’s more of a product/architecture tradeoff than a verifiable correctness defect in the new design.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx:43 — error` is never destructured from `useGetGrafanaGroupsQuery`, so an actual query error (vs. still-loading) is indistinguishable from "no data yet" and only produces the same generic "Failed to load rules" alert with no error detail, unlike the deleted `GrafanaRuleLoader`'s `RulerRuleLoadingError` which surfaced the real error object.

adjudication.rationale: In GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx the hook call `useGetGrafanaGroupsQuery(...)` is destructured only as `{ data: promResponse, isLoading: isPromResponseLoading }` (no `error`). The component then renders a skeleton while loading, and renders the same generic `<Alert ...>` when `!promResponse`, which would also be the state on a query error. This is a verifiable regression in error surfacing compared to the deleted GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx which explicitly handled `rulerRuleGroupError || promRuleGroupError` via `RulerRuleLoadingError` and passed through the actual error object. It’s not a functional correctness break, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded loss of error detail/diagnostics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx:66 — Removing the ruler-only "Creating" placeholder (previously shown immediately from the strongly-consistent Ruler write while Prometheus scrape lags) means newly created/updated rules now simply do not appear in the list at all until the next Prometheus poll cycle, with no loading/pending indicator to bridge the eventual-consistency gap.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the previous bridging logic in `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx` that rendered ruler-only rules as `RuleOperation.Creating` (and prom-only as deleting): the ruler query (`useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery`), `matchRules(...)`, and the `if (!promRule) { ... operation={RuleOperation.Creating} }` branch were deleted, and rendering is now solely `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules.map(...)`. Therefore, if a rule exists in the Ruler response but is not yet present in the Prometheus groups response, it will not be shown at all. However, the finding asserts this gap definitively exists (“Prometheus scrape lags”); the diff also contained prior commentary suggesting strong consistency, so whether this is an actual defect vs. an intentional removal of now-unneeded fallback cannot be proven from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:296 — isProvisionedPromRule` (and the `isProvisioned: Boolean(provenance)` badge in GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx:29) gate immutability on a brand-new `provenance` field added to `GrafanaPromRuleDTOBase` in this diff; previously this same protection was sourced from the Ruler API (`grafana_alert.provenance`), and in the new Prometheus-only list view the Ruler path is skipped entirely, so if the backend Prometheus rules endpoint doesn't reliably populate `provenance`, provisioned/immutable rules become editable, deletable, pausable, and permanently-deletable from the rule list with no compensating check

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a behavioral shift in how “provisioned/immutable” is determined for Grafana Prometheus rules when the list view no longer fetches the Ruler API: GrafanaGroupLoader now renders only Prometheus rules (promResponse.data.groups...rules) and no longer matches with rulerResponse / grafana_alert.provenance. In the new abilities path (useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities), immutability depends on `isProvisionedPromRule(rule)` which checks `Boolean(promRule.provenance)`, and the UI badge in GrafanaRuleListItem uses `isProvisioned: Boolean(provenance)` from the same Prom rule. This creates a concrete risk that if the Prometheus endpoint doesn’t populate `provenance`, provisioned rules would be treated as mutable in the list view. However, the diff does not let us verify whether the backend endpoint reliably provides `provenance`, so we can’t confirm an actual defect—only a diff-grounded, specific edge-case/compatibility concern created by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rule-viewer/AlertRuleMenu.tsx:78 — canPause`/`canDelete`/`canDuplicate`/`canSilence`/`canExport` are computed by OR-ing two independently-derived ability results (Ruler-based and Grafana-Prometheus-DTO-based); this "fail open on either path" pattern means any future loosening or bug in either of the two now-duplicated permission-derivation implementations silently grants the action rather than being caught, since only one path needs to say "allowed"

adjudication.rationale: In AlertRuleMenu.tsx the new logic derives abilities from two different hooks (useRulerRuleAbilities and useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities) and then computes canPause/canDelete/canDuplicate/canSilence/canExport by OR-ing the two results, e.g. `const canPause = (pauseSupported && pauseAllowed) || (grafanaPauseSupported && grafanaPauseAllowed);`. This is verifiably a “permit if either path permits” pattern. The finding’s concern (duplicated authorization logic where any future bug/loosening in either path could silently grant actions) is a real, diff-grounded design/security-review issue, but the diff does not demonstrate an actual current incorrect permission grant—this behavior may be intentional to support list-view without ruler API calls.
